purpose: Per-tool acceptance for project-owned persistent environments. Each row states what was exercised and HOW STRONG the evidence is, so nothing reads as verified because a mock agreed with itself.

evidenceLevels.real-guest: Exercised against a real systemd-nspawn machine on a host prepared by tests/plugins/nspawnProofHost.mjs. There is no private engine to create and reset for a machine, so the suite refuses to run on a host whose teardown is not armed.
evidenceLevels.unit: Exercised against in-process fakes only. Proves the logic, not that the guest behaves this way.
evidenceLevels.unverified: No acceptance yet at any level, or only indirect coverage.

rows.capability: create/start/inspect a project environment
rows.notes: systemd guest booted by systemd-nspawn under a machine-scoped unit, on a disk materialized from the published root filesystem its record names, with a virtual ethernet the host guard keeps off the host itself.

rows.capability: stop/start restart preserves rootfs, home, workspace, data
cgroup limits applied (cpu.max, memory.max, pids.max)
snapshot then restore into a fresh generation
rows.notes: Was the long-standing blocker; restore now rebuilds the volume and retains worktree metadata.

rows.capability: delete environment and release its resources
generation mismatch refused
member revocation cancels that account's guest leases
rows.notes: Now exercised mid-flight against a real guest: a second member's command is running when the revocation lands, and the kill is judged by the command never reaching its own last statement and returning in seconds rather than its 300-second sleep, because systemd reports a unit stopped by SIGTERM as a clean stop. The revoked account is then refused while the project keeps serving its remaining member.

rows.capability: shell command through the bootstrap frame (duplex stdin preserved)
rows.notes: Two-write delayed echo confirmed later stdin frames are delivered.

rows.capability: argv launch with PATH resolved inside the guest
rows.notes: lspManaged covers argv launch and guest PATH resolution through an in-process project provider; no nspawn guest suite covers it yet.

rows.capability: cancellation kills the guest unit and its descendants
execution uses the environment's whole pid budget
rows.notes: TasksMax=infinity; guest systemd otherwise capped a unit at 15% of the declared limit.

rows.capability: background/foreground/cwd/output-limit behaviour in a guest
rows.notes: Real Bash tool: foreground in the guest cwd, guest filesystem, non-zero exit reported, oversized output truncated, background run tracked by ListProcesses and killed by KillProcess.

rows.capability: write, read, and version-conflict refusal
rows.notes: expectedVersion null means must-not-exist; stale version refused.

rows.capability: read bounded by the guest transfer limit
rows.notes: Managed LSP asked for 2 MiB against a 512 KiB bound and every check silently degraded.

rows.capability: chunked upload protocol and completion metadata
rows.notes: Covered by environmentLifecycle at protocol level: begin, chunked write, abort, commit, the actor and generation bounds on each, and the fixed answer a failing guest upload gets. A machine execution carries no completion-cwd capture and the client refuses to arm one, which nspawnRuntime pins.

rows.capability: Read/Edit/Write/Glob/Grep/ListDir/FileInfo against a managed project
rows.notes: The registered plugin tools' own execute() against a container: Write, Read, Edit, ListDir, FileInfo, Glob, Grep. The host path guard is asserted never to be consulted.

rows.capability: GitStatus and worktrees in a managed project
rows.notes: GitStatus tool and worktree lifecycle both exercised against a guest.

rows.capability: ShareFile resolves a managed guest path
rows.notes: ShareFile reads guest bytes through the provider; relative path and missing provider both refuse without a host read.

rows.capability: the plan mirror under a managed project
rows.notes: Plan written through the central guest writer and submitted by ExitPlanMode; a write outside the artifact prefix is refused. Transcripts and share links are NOT covered here.

rows.capability: project preview binding serves over a unix socket and releases
rows.notes: Real HTTP 200; socket gone after release.

rows.capability: install a language server into the guest and find it on PATH
rows.notes: lspManaged covers installation commands and PATH lookup through an in-process project provider; no nspawn guest suite covers it yet.

rows.capability: diagnostics: error reported, then clean after the fix
rows.notes: lspManaged covers diagnostic publication and clearing through an in-process project provider; no nspawn guest suite covers it yet.

rows.capability: server lifetime owned by the lease, not a host pid watchdog
rows.notes: lspManaged covers the lease-owned server lifecycle and refuses host-pid ownership through an in-process project provider.

rows.capability: headless Chromium renders in the guest
rows.notes: Engine level only: proves Chromium starts in the container. The browser plugin no longer runs a browser inside a project environment, so there is no tool surface here to cover.

rows.capability: upload/download/save/listing against a managed project
rows.notes: Managed editor suites cover chunked upload, raw download, range requests and version-guarded saves through an in-process project provider.

rows.capability: project MCP install, reconnect, schema visibility
rows.notes: Install, reconnect, call, remove and the wrong-project/no-member refusals run against a real guest. Schema VISIBILITY was a separate defect and is covered by mcpPlugin: a project-bound stdio server can be stored at instance scope, where its tool names, descriptions and input schemas were composed for every account on the instance. The declaration now carries its project id and the session composer drops it outside that project.

rows.capability: scheduled turn scoping to a managed project
rows.notes: cronManaged covers projectCheck execution, failures and membership refusal through an in-process project provider. Scheduling cadence stays with the cronjob suites.

rows.capability: delegated scope cannot retarget or enumerate projects
rows.notes: Covered by delegatedTurnWire over the delegation contract, which is where retargeting would have to happen. A guest adds nothing: the refusal is decided before any environment is resolved.

rows.capability: a managed conversation refuses its turn when no provider resolves
rows.notes: Observed for real when a stale bundled plugin made the whole sandbox control unresolvable.

rows.capability: Git and publishing credential separation
rows.notes: Two halves, both verified. The guest exec unit carries only PATH, LANG and its own systemd bookkeeping, daemon environment sentinels including GH_TOKEN are absent from it, and the pinned executor fails the run outright if such a credential ever appears in the environment of any process the machine client spawns (managedToolCallers.nspawn). Authenticated publishing IS supported and is not a gap: publishManaged builds a git bundle inside the guest, reads it out through projectFiles, validates and stages it on the HOST, and pushes from there with the account's token, which githubStaging asserts never appears in the managed launch. What remains forbidden is injecting a token into the guest and pushing from it. LIMIT: no push to a real remote is exercised anywhere, because that would publish.

rows.capability: codebase indexing/search inside a managed project
rows.notes: The codebase suite covers provider-backed list/read operations, stable managed project keys, membership checks, host isolation, scheduled-index skipping and project-removal pruning through an in-process project provider.

rows.capability: central personal integrations (onedrive, github, voice-bot, image-gen, image-edit, todo, stats, skills, web)
rows.notes: Scope regression rather than live proof: driving real external writes would need credentials and publishes nobody authorized. The pinned property is that these tools stay ACCOUNT-scoped and that project scoping neither narrows them nor widens them to another account. Their external behaviour against real services is NOT covered here.

rows.capability: another project's identity cannot reach this environment
rows.notes: Denied at the project boundary, not by the file simply being absent.

rows.capability: a path the guest protocol cannot express safely is refused
rows.notes: The container is the boundary, so a guest path is not refused merely for sitting outside /workspace.

rows.capability: office preview converters in a guest
rows.notes: editorManagedOperations covers converter dispatch, scratch cleanup, unsupported files and the missing-converter response through an in-process project provider.

rows.capability: ShareImage resolves a managed guest path
rows.notes: A real PNG written into the project comes back byte-identical in conversation storage, verified by its header and full contents, and a text file named .png is refused on its sniffed bytes. No longer claimed by association with ShareFile.

rows.capability: conversation transcripts and tool-result spills under a managed project
rows.notes: The cold clearing pass runs with a real BrainStore and the real provider; the spill is read back OUT of the guest, the transcript row names the guest path, the newest turn stays intact and nothing lands in the host spill directory. Transcripts themselves are central storage with no guest side, so only the spill has a guest journey to verify.

rows.capability: cost of one guest file operation
rows.notes: What the count is: managedFileOperationCost pins one 'stat' at exactly four host subprocesses — the unit half of the ownership proof, the machine-manager half, the guest launcher and the release probe. The historical figures it replaced were measured on the container runtime, where the same operation cost 6689 ms across 57 invocations and 5681 ms across 41 after a duplicated ownership verification per release was removed; the machine runtime's own measured round trip is in environmentNspawnProof, whose bound is a median under 500 ms against that runtime's measured 856. The mask/stop/mask/verify/unmask choreography and the ownership check remain, because they are correctness properties.
